question:
What is the standard Japanese pitch accent pattern of 「弟」?

Answer Choices:
A. Heiban
B. Atamadaka
C. Nakadaka
D. Odaka
E. Heiban or Nakadaka

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The word 「弟」 (おとうと) consists of 4 morae. In standard Tokyo Japanese, its pitch pattern is L-H-L-L (i.e., the pitch rises on the second mora and falls immediately after it). This matches the definition of nakadaka accent. Therefore the answer is C.

(The pattern is fixed in dictionaries such as NHK and Shin Meikai; variant pronunciations are not recognized as standard.)

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Nakadaka

「弟」 (otōto) is a 4-mora word (o-to-u-to). Standard dictionaries (NHK, Shin-Meikai, etc.) mark it with a pitch drop after the second mora, producing the pattern L-H-L-L. This is the textbook definition of nakadaka accent for a 4-mora noun. It is not heiban (which would stay L-H-H-H), not atamadaka (H-L-L-L), and not odaka (L-H-H-H with a drop only when a particle follows). The pattern is stable across common corpora and does not vary between heiban and nakadaka.
